reasons: Section 18.9 gives both Parties (including us as Ono) a consent-free assignment right to an entity acquiring substantially all business or assets by merger or acquisition, so there is no blanket prohibition and no walk-away trigger; the deterministic check confirms the successor carve-out is present.

Affiliate assignment is permitted subject to mutual consent 'not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed', which squarely matches the fallback position ('mutual right to assign to successors...; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld'), so the clause is correctly classified compliant-at-fallback rather than a deviation.

Section 18.10 imposes only firewall obligations on a Change in Control of the counterparty (Array) and no provision gives the counterparty any termination, re-pricing or renegotiation right on our change of control, satisfying the rule's change-of-control requirement.

Shortfalls versus preferred wording (consent needed for affiliate assignment, unqualified consent standard for Third Party assignments, tax-consequences proviso) are mutual and correctly treated as minor sub-elements noted in the rationale, not redlined.
Consistent with a compliant finding, the redline is unchanged from the original paragraphs and no counterparty comment is proposed.
